tagline.text: The Philippines' cowboy island stages a cattle-handling contest and street festival every April

location.label: Location
location.text: Masbate City, around the Grand Rodeo Arena and the city center

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~4,000 (per person per day, rough estimate for lodging, meals and local transport; airfare, ferry and tickets not included)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Masbate Airport (Moises R. Espinosa Airport, MBT)

children.text: The Masbate Rodeo (Rodeo Masbateño) began in 1993 and is held every April in Masbate City, the best-known rodeo festival in the Philippines. Lasso and bull-riding contests, a cattle drive and a street barn-dance competition all come together in one city, so you can see a ranching culture that is rarely part of an ordinary trip.

Masbate is an island province in the Bicol region and one of the leading cattle-raising areas in the Philippines. Ranching took hold in the 19th century when forest land was turned into grassland, and beef raised here is said to have supplied Manila, Cavite and other nearby provinces. Where there are ranches and cowboys, a rodeo tends to follow, and everyday cattle-handling skills naturally grew into competitions. The result is Rodeo Masbateño, held every April in Masbate City.

The festival was started in 1993 by then-Governor Emilio Espinosa Jr. together with local ranchers and businessmen, with the aim of putting Masbate on the map and reviving tourism. In the same year a group of ranchers organized as Rodeo Masbateño, Inc. (RMI) institutionalized the event. It was reported that on September 2, 2002, the president of the time proclaimed Masbate the "Rodeo Capital of the Philippines." Wikipedia lists the city's nickname as the "Rodeo Capital of Southeast Asia," so both expressions are in use. The DOT Bicol regional director has said that in Bicol the festival is second in popularity only to the Peñafrancia Festival.

What travelers feel most strongly here is that real daily work becomes the sport. Lassoing a steer from horseback, wrestling cattle on foot, staying on a bull's back and running a load-carrying relay all come straight out of ranch work. The festival director has made the same point, describing rodeo as a showcase of animal-handling skills that grew out of ranch chores. At first only men competed, but women now take part too, and in 2016 a special bull-riding event for women was held. Hundreds of horses in the parade and a cattle drive through city streets set this festival apart from others in the Philippines.

This guide is for travelers who want to visit Masbate City during the April festival. Events, competition formats and schedules change a little each year, and the edition number grows every year (27th in 2023, 30th in 2026). For exact dates and programs, check the latest announcements from Rodeo Masbateño or the Masbate city and provincial tourism offices. Flying from Manila is the easiest way to get to Masbate, but flights are limited, so book airfare and lodging early for festival time.
The Masbate Grand Rodeo Arena in Masbate City is described as the only permanent rodeo arena in the country. After the opening parade the competition program is held here, and one report says about
2,000 people
watched when the 2014 festival opened. Entrance fees and seating zones differ each year, so check locally.

The National Finals bring together cowboy and cowgirl teams from all over the country. In 2016, 12 teams competed in the professional category and 14 in the school category. Events include cattle wrestling and lassoing on foot, steer lassoing on horseback, casting down, two-person and four-person carambola, bull riding and the load-carrying relay. Special events such as bronco riding, bull riding for women and team penning are also held.
During the festival, herds of cattle are driven through the city streets. In 2014 the cattle drive and a cattle horse team penning contest were held on the same day,
April 9
, and a daily cattle drive was part of the 2023 program. You can watch along city streets, so check local announcements for times and routes.

At the opening, a parade sets out from around the Social Center Triangle downtown, passes along the main roads and enters the arena. In 2014 at least 45 contingents joined the march, and in 2023 hundreds of horses from various ranches took part, with a cowboy statue unveiled in front of the provincial capitol. The opening parade on April 13, 2026 was also reported to have ended at the same arena.

blocks.title: Street barn dance and Mr. & Ms. Rodeo

children.text: A street barn-dance competition is held on city streets, along with a cowgirl search and the Mr. & Ms. Rodeo contest. In 2014 both were held on the same day,
April 10
. Even if you do not watch the contests, it is a good way to enjoy the evening street atmosphere.

blocks.title: Beef cooking contest and livestock fair

children.text: In 2014 a beef cooking contest (
April 11
), a trade fair and agribusiness roadshow, and a livestock show (
April 8–13

) were held together, and the revived livestock auction was expected to draw buyers from Isabela, Batangas and Pangasinan. In 2023 a beef cooking contest for young chefs was held too. The lineup may change from year to year.

Between events you can visit places such as the Cathedral-Parish of Saint Anthony of Padua, the Coastal Resource Management Interpretative Center (CRMIC), the Pawa Mangrove Nature Park and the Buntod Sand Bar and marine sanctuary. The Pagdayao Festival on June 13 for Saint Anthony of Padua and the Lapay Bantigue dance festival on September 30 for the city anniversary take place in other seasons.

items.title: Two-day festival route
items.subtitle: City and parade on the first day, contests on the second

children.text: Fly in from Manila on a morning flight to Masbate Airport, leave your bags at the hotel and walk around the city center.
See the cathedral and the city waterfront, then have lunch at a nearby restaurant.
If the day's program includes a cattle drive or a livestock show, watch it in the city. Confirm the schedule through the announcements of the day.
Watch an evening event such as the street barn dance or a cowgirl search, and try beef dishes at a local restaurant.
On the morning of day two, go to the Grand Rodeo Arena and watch the morning contests. Choose a seat on the shaded side.
After lunch, keep watching the afternoon contests (bull riding, carambola and more), then fly home that evening or the next day.
Flights are limited, so a same-day round trip is hard. During the finals the last day of contests can run long, so leave plenty of time before your return flight.

items.title: Three-day extended route
items.subtitle: The festival plus Masbate's sea and mangroves

children.text: Arrive on day one, see the city and the cathedral, and watch a street event in the evening.
On day two, watch the contests in the morning, then spend the afternoon on a short trip to a nearby shoreline or the Pawa Mangrove Nature Park.
On the morning of day three, take a tour to the Buntod Sand Bar or a marine sanctuary (check locally whether it is running), then fly back in the afternoon.
Sea tours are canceled depending on waves and weather, so keep a backup plan.

Flights from Manila to Masbate Airport (Moises R. Espinosa Airport) are known to be operated by Cebgo, a Cebu Pacific affiliate, in the morning. The airport is inside the city, so the ride to your hotel is short.
The number of flights and the timetable change every season, and seats fill quickly during the festival. Check the airline's announcements and book early.
Check the airline's website for current flight times and fares.
From Manila you can take the South Road to Pio Duran in Albay or to Pilar or Bulan in Sorsogon, then cross to Masbate by RORO ferry or fastcraft. Wikipedia gives about
2 hours 15 minutes
by RORO or fastcraft and about
3 hours
by small motorized boat.
Large ships sail from the Port of Manila to Masbate and are said to take about
16–18 hours
. There are also sea routes from Dalahican Port in Lucena in southern Luzon and from Allen in Northern Samar.
Tricycles and motorcycle taxis are the main local transport. The arena is close to most lodging, so you can walk or take a tricycle.
During the festival roads can be congested or closed, so allow extra travel time.

Rodeo Masbateño is usually held in mid-April, and in some years livestock shows and events begin as early as late March. In 2014 it ran from March 30 to April 13, the 2016 National Finals took place on April 12–17, and in 2023 it ran until April 16.

Masbate City's dry season is known to run from February to June, with the rainy season starting in July. April is dry and good for watching outdoor contests, but midday is very hot. The mean temperature is about

Masbate City has hotels and small guesthouses, but they are the first to fill up during the festival. Book lodging early along with your flight, and choose a place with easy transport to the arena. Names and rates change a lot from season to season, so check recent reviews on a booking site.

Masbate is cattle country, so there are plenty of chances to eat beef dishes. The festival even holds a beef cooking contest where you can see local cooking. At restaurants and markets in town, eat where you can see hygiene and prices for yourself. Food at stalls around the arena can spoil quickly at midday, so be careful.
The arena gets strong sun, so bring a hat, sunscreen, water and a fan.
Flights are limited, so secure your flight and lodging first, then plan the rest.
The schedule changes every year, so check the organizers' announcements (RMI, city and provincial tourism offices) before you arrive.
Cattle and horses can move close to you in the arena, so take photos from outside the safety line.
During the cattle drive, do not stand in the middle of the road; watch from the sidewalk.
Phone signal and internet can be weak in places, so save maps and bookings in advance.
Carry plenty of cash. Small shops and tricycles often accept cash only.
Under animal welfare rules, animals are reportedly checked by a veterinarian before, during and after the event. Do not touch or provoke the animals.
Masbate is known as an area that has had problems with political violence. In election periods or other unsettled times, check your government's travel advisory and local announcements before you go.
Contest schedules and events change every year, so the dates in this guide are examples from past editions. Check the latest schedule.
During the festival, lodging and flights fill quickly and prices can rise.
Midday outdoor contests carry a risk of heat illness. Drink water often and rest in the shade.
Because the event involves animals, concerns about animal welfare have been raised. Check the organizers' safety and animal protection guidance before attending.
Ferries can be canceled by weather, so leave extra room in your return plan.
